name: Rice (Local)
description: Locally milled rice from northern states such as Kebbi and Ebonyi. Price follows harvest size and transport cost to Lagos.

name: Rice (Imported)
description: Foreign parboiled rice sold in Lagos markets. Its price moves closely with the dollar exchange rate.

name: Maize (White)
description: Dry white maize grain used for pap, flour and animal feed. Price drops after harvest and rises in the lean months.

name: Sliced Bread
description: Factory-baked bread. Wheat is imported, so the exchange rate and energy costs matter most.

name: Spaghetti
description: Packaged pasta made from imported wheat. Price follows the exchange rate and factory costs.

name: Beans (Brown)
description: Brown beans (Oloyin) from the north. Supply depends on harvest and the long trip to Lagos.

name: Beans (White)
description: White beans (Ife Brown and similar) from the north. Price tracks harvest size and transport.

name: Yam
description: Yam tubers from the middle belt. Prices peak mid-year and fall once new yam arrives from August.

name: Irish Potato
description: Potatoes grown mainly around Jos. Price depends on supply from the plateau and transport.

name: Sweet Potato
description: Sweet potato from southwestern and northern farms. Cheap and fairly steady through the year.

name: Garri (White)
description: Fermented cassava granules, a staple across Lagos. Price follows cassava supply.

name: Garri (Yellow)
description: Cassava granules fried with palm oil. Moves with cassava and palm oil supply.

name: Tomato
description: Fresh tomatoes trucked from Kano, Kaduna and Jos. Fragile and seasonal, so price swings a lot.

name: Onion
description: Red onions from the north, mostly Sokoto and Kano. Price rises when stored stock runs low.

name: Fresh Pepper
description: Tatashe and rodo peppers from farms around Lagos and the north. Very sensitive to season and transport.

name: Carrot
description: Carrots grown on the Jos plateau. Price follows supply and the cost of moving it south.

name: Plantain (Unripe)
description: Unripe plantain from the southwest and south-south. Fairly steady, with small seasonal moves.

name: Beef (Boneless)
description: Boneless cow meat from Lagos abattoirs. Cattle come from the north, so transport and general inflation matter.

name: Whole Chicken
description: Frozen or fresh whole chicken. Feed is largely imported, and demand jumps at Christmas.

name: Frozen Fish (Mackerel)
description: Imported frozen mackerel (Titus). Price follows the exchange rate and import costs.

name: Eggs
description: Table eggs from poultry farms around Lagos and Ogun. Feed costs drive the price, with a bump in December.

name: Vegetable Oil
description: Refined cooking oil. Raw materials are partly imported, so the exchange rate has a strong effect.

name: Palm Oil
description: Red palm oil from the south. Output is seasonal and transport adds to the cost.

name: Sugar
description: Granulated sugar, mostly refined from imported raw sugar. Follows the exchange rate closely.

name: Powdered Milk
description: Imported milk powder in tins. Price is driven by the dollar and import costs.
